text:
alex_k: thinking out loud — we need to finalize the ranking API contract for the new ordering endpoint. specifically: what score format do we return and what are sane per-request limits?

maria_g: +1 we should make this ergonomic for product teams. current internal variants: raw logits, calibrated 0..1 probs, and a relative score normalized per-batch. tricky tradeoffs. :thinking_face:

sahil: my hot take: return `score` as 0..1 by default and `raw` only when `debug=true`. most clients want an intuitive higher-is-better number.

eva_l: worried about calibration — different models produce different distributions, so 0..1 can be misleading unless we calibrate per-model. calibration costs ops.

jordan: could we expose `score_type` in the response and a header `x-score-model` so downstream can decide? e.g. `score_type: probability|logit|relative`.

alex_k: proposal: default response includes `score` (0..1) and `meta` list of tags like `score_type=prob` or `score_type=relative`. add `raw_logit` only in debug. keep default payload small.

maria_g: also think we should document sort order explicitly: `higher score = better`. avoid ambiguity.

sahil: on limits — recommend default `max_candidates=50`, soft cap 200, and a hard reject at 1000. large requests kill latency. we should also expose per-team quota (tokens + candidate count).

eva_l: is 50 enough for search use-cases? some customers send 100-200. maybe default 100, but recommend 50 for lowest-latency tier.

jordan: routing policy interplay: if candidate_count > 200, auto-route to cheaper cross-encoder (lower quality) or queue for batch processing. should be configurable per-project.

alex_k: ops note: we need telemetry for candidate_count distribution, score histograms per-model, and P50/P95 latency. this helps detect score shifts after rollouts.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: canary rollout of `rerank-v2` to 5% traffic at 2026-03-05T14:22:00Z

maria_g: rollout UX requirement — console should show baseline score distribution vs canary, and an automatic regression alert if mean score shifts > 0.05 or top-1 churn > 10%.

sahil: and a way to compare top-k differences for sample prompts. product wants to see human-visible diffs, not just numbers.

eva_l: API shape suggestion: request: `{"model":"auto|rerank-v2", "candidates": [...], "return_debug": false}`. response snippet: ```json
{"results":[{"id":"c1","score":0.82},{"id":"c2","score":0.11}],"model":"rerank-v2","score_type":"prob"}```

jordan: minor: should we include per-item `explain` only when `return_debug`? that explainer can be a small token map. otherwise payloads get huge.

alex_k: agree. keep explain behind debug. also add `fallback_model` array in response if we routed to a fallback due to capacity: `fallback_model:["rerank-mini"]`.

maria_g: about quotas — we need UI knobs: per-project candidate-rate limit and burst size. and billing metric should be `candidate_units` (= sum candidates * weight(model)).

sahil: weight(model) idea is good. heavy models count as 4 units per candidate, cheap ones 1. makes reserved capacity sensible.

eva_l: telemetry keys: `route`, `model`, `candidate_count`, `p95_latency`, `score_mean`, `score_std`, `top1_churn`. we should stream these to console and to alerts.

jordan: open question: should the API accept logits and do normalization server-side for ensembles? some teams might want to submit pre-scored items.

alex_k: we can support `client_scores` input, but we must require `score_type` in the input and then we will run final merge logic. but that complicates verification. maybe v1: only accept raw candidates + optional client_score with `merge_policy=trust|recalc`.

maria_g: UX on console: when you create a rollout, let users set `score_compatibility_threshold` so we auto-fallback if the canary produces scores out-of-range. saves us from silent regressions.

sahil: final ask for contract: clearly document: default `max_candidates=100`, hard limit 1000, default `score` 0..1, `raw_logit` only with debug, `return_debug` opt-in, `model:auto` routing, fallback metadata in response, and telemetry fields.

eva_l: +1 but change default to 50 for low-latency tier. maybe docs show tiers: low-latency (50), balanced (100), throughput (200).

alex_k: ok i'll draft the RFC with these tiers and API samples. will include examples for console rollout checks and example prometheus metrics.

jordan: thanks — @maria_g @sahil @eva_l @infra-bot please review RFC when posted. :eyes: 

maria_g: thanks, will review. :thumbsup:
